identityReview: Rishi Sunak, born 12 May 1980 in Southampton, Conservative politician and current Richmond and Northallerton MP. Former prime minister, chancellor and opposition leader; party leadership and premiership started on different October 2022 dates and ended on different 2024 dates. Oxford undergraduate degree and Stanford MBA are distinct from honorary titles. Outside corporate roles are not current government offices.
lifeStatusEvidence: Hansard records his actual 12 November 2026 Commons question on Northallerton station parking and the Leader of the House’s reply. This is a recent parliamentary intervention, not a scheduled appearance, an undated biography or an inference from absence of an obituary.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read government and parliamentary biographies, financial-interest register, Oxford college and school biographies, independent birth/education profile, original Treasury script, Commons Library analysis, Supreme Court press summary and current Hansard exchange. Read Commons, original Flickr photograph metadata, official account permission statement and the photo’s Creative Commons licence deed.
corrections: Read the government biography: prime minister 25 October 2022–5 July 2024; chancellor 13 February 2020–5 July 2022; chief secretary 24 July 2019–13 February 2020; parliamentary under-secretary 9 January 2018–24 July 2019. Education lists Winchester, Oxford PPE and Stanford MBA as a Fulbright scholar. The profile is a historical ministerial biography, not evidence of a current premiership.

Read the current parliamentary career record: Conservative MP from 7 May 2015; three elections in Richmond (Yorks), with that representation ending at dissolution on 30 May 2024; Richmond and Northallerton from the 4 July 2024 election. Conservative leader 24 October 2022–2 November 2024; official opposition leader 5 July–2 November 2024. Party election and prime-ministerial appointment are separate dates. Boundary change is not treated as a party switch or loss of parliamentary career.

Read biographical sections stating birth in Southampton on 12 May 1980, Oxford first-class graduation in 2001 and Stanford MBA in 2006. Birth and MBA year are secondary-source facts, corroborated in broad educational outline by official government and university biographies. No original civil record or degree certificate was inspected. Peripheral family finances and unsourced evaluative claims are not reproduced.

Read Lincoln College’s alumni announcement: matriculation in 1998, first-class PPE graduation in 2001, subsequent Stanford MBA, financial career and 2015 Richmond election. The college’s hopes for his premiership are attributed opinion, not an assessment of accomplished policy outcomes. This is a historical announcement rather than current office evidence.

Read Treasury’s original script published 20 March 2020, explicitly marked as possibly differing from delivery. It announces employer grants for furloughed workers, initially 80% of pay up to £2,500 monthly, backdated to 1 March, initially at least three months. Application infrastructure and first payments were still prospective. The profile does not claim the script proves every spoken word, immediate disbursement, universal eligibility irrespective of scheme rules, or a measured total of jobs saved.

Read Commons Library briefing: political agreement announced by Sunak and von der Leyen on 27 February 2023; trade, VAT, regulation and Stormont Brake arrangements required subsequent procedures. The briefing still describes the 24 March Joint Committee meeting prospectively; it is not used as proof that meeting occurred. The separate European Commission chronology could not be fetched; EUR-Lex extraction returned no substantive text. Accordingly, no exact later adoption or implementation date is asserted.

Read Supreme Court’s own press-summary PDF for the 15 November 2023 AAA judgment. The unanimous decision upholds unlawfulness because of real refoulement and ill-treatment risks under the evidence and arrangements then examined. The MEDP memorandum predated Sunak’s premiership, dating to April 2022. This is judicial review of a policy, not his personal criminal conviction. The full judgment and later Rwanda legislation were not exhaustively reviewed; no assertion that the 2023 ruling alone resolves all later measures is made.

Read current members’ interests entries: senior advisor to both Anthropic and Microsoft from 9 October 2025, registered 29 October. The Anthropic remuneration agreement has a different September date, which is not substituted for the role start. Registration confirms disclosed outside work; approval advice alone would not prove commencement. Private/contact addresses, pay calculations and speculative conflicts are not included. Other recorded roles and all payments are not exhaustively audited.

Read actual Hansard exchange of 12 November 2026, Sunak’s question and Alan Campbell’s reply: Northallerton station parking, a meeting he said he convened with council, mayor’s office and TransPennine Express, and clarification of the local transport grant. Campbell acknowledged letters to departments and offered follow-up. This supplies recent actual parliamentary activity, not merely a future agenda. Neither speaker establishes final funding approval or completed construction.

Read Blavatnik biography identifying prior Goldman Sachs and The Children’s Investment Fund employment and co-founding an investment firm, with current Richmond and Northallerton representation. Employment dates, exact co-founder ownership shares and a professorial appointment are not inferred. The university affiliation does not itself confer a new academic degree.

Read office homepage date and description, but article extraction supplied no substantive transcript and embedded video was not watched. The biography uses Hansard for recent activity instead.
Search preview only; open failed. Not used to assert completed 24 March adoption.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original birth/degree documents, exhaustive employment or payments audit, complete 2023 judgment and later statutory review, original parliamentary video, portrait pixels or independently retrieved OGL document. The Commons Library historical briefing is not treated as a current implementation ledger. Corporate disclosures do not by themselves establish misconduct.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons and official Number 10 Flickr source: photograph taken 24 November 2022, Flickr uploaded 7 June 2023, Commons transfer and later levels/color adjustment on 9 June 2023. Current Commons file 3888×5832, about 2.16 MB. Official account states OGL 3.0 except where otherwise stated; the photo-level licence link resolves to CC BY-NC-ND 2.0. Commons acknowledges the mismatch and relies on the account-wide statement. No assumption is made that the general statement overrides a photo-specific exception or that the edited file is publishable under ND terms. National Archives licence URL returned 403; Commons licence summary read. Original download failed with curl exit 22, 403/HTTP000; no cache directory or visible pixels. Identity, natural color, sharpness, alterations and licence handling remain unverified.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed for birth and education, financial career, current constituency and old boundaries, party leadership versus premiership, 2020 scheme announcement versus grants, 80%/£2,500 initial support and 1 March backdating, political Windsor agreement versus later implementation, historical Rwanda ruling versus personal criminal liability or later legislation, 2024 separate office end dates, 2025 disclosed corporate role start dates and actual 12 November 2026 parliamentary question.
